package_info.package_manager: system package manager (e.g., apt, yum, pacman), source distribution
package_info.package_versions: all versions (distrotech/cups-filters, OpenPrinting/cups-filters, cups-browsed, libcupsfilters, libppd)
package_info.why_malicious: The packages contain critical vulnerabilities that allow unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) through network-exposed CUPS services. Attackers can exploit these flaws by sending specially crafted network requests to the CUPS service, typically on UDP port 631 or via DNS-SD, resulting in arbitrary code execution on affected systems. These vulnerabilities are present in all previous versions and can be exploited remotely if the CUPS service is enabled and accessible, posing a severe risk of full system compromise.

execution_context.trigger: Receipt of a specially crafted unauthenticated network request (runtime, during CUPS service operation)
execution_context.file_location: CUPS service daemon (cupsd), network-exposed process (typically /usr/sbin/cupsd or equivalent)
required_permissions: filesystem (to write/read files as part of print job processing or exploit payloads)
process execution (to spawn child processes or execute attacker-controlled code)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: N/A (The report does not provide a specific code snippet, but describes a vulnerability in the CUPS service that allows unauthenticated remote code execution when a specially crafted network request is received on UDP port 631 or via DNS-SD.)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, upon receiving a specially crafted unauthenticated network request on UDP port 631 or via DNS-SD, the vulnerable code path in the CUPS service processes the request, leading to execution of attacker-controlled code on the system, resulting in remote code execution and potential full system compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing unauthenticated remote code execution via a network-exposed service is highly suspicious and dangerous, as it enables attackers to compromise systems without any credentials or user interaction.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal CUPS operation should only process authenticated and well-formed print service requests, never execute arbitrary code from unauthenticated or malformed network sources, and should not allow remote code execution under any circumstances.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate remote print job submission or management should require authentication and should never result in arbitrary code execution; only print data should be processed, not executable payloads.
key_indicators: Unauthenticated network access to the CUPS service on UDP port 631 or via DNS-SD
Abnormal or unexpected child process creation by the cupsd daemon
Execution of code or binaries not associated with normal print job processing
Unusual file writes or modifications by the CUPS service, especially in /tmp or other writable directories
Modifications to CUPS configuration files without administrative action

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted unauthenticated network request to the CUPS service (typically on UDP port 631 or via DNS-SD).
attack_chain.leads_to: Triggering the vulnerable code path in the CUPS service.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable code path in the CUPS service processes the malicious request and executes attacker-controlled code on the system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on the target system, potentially leading to full system compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Unauthenticated or malformed network requests to the CUPS service resulting in abnormal process behavior
Unexpected child process creation by the cupsd daemon
Unusual file writes or modifications by the CUPS service, especially in /tmp or other writable directories
Execution of binaries or scripts by cupsd not associated with normal print job processing
file_indicators: Unexpected binaries or scripts created in /tmp or other writable directories by the CUPS service
Modifications to CUPS configuration files (e.g., /etc/cups/cupsd.conf) without administrative action
Presence of files with suspicious names or permissions in directories writable by the CUPS service
network_indicators: Inbound unauthenticated traffic to UDP port 631 from untrusted or external sources
Unusual DNS-SD traffic targeting the CUPS service
Outbound connections initiated by the CUPS service to external IP addresses, especially following receipt of suspicious network requests
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthenticated or malformed network requests to the CUPS service, particularly on UDP port 631 or via DNS-SD. Use intrusion detection systems to flag exploit attempts targeting CUPS vulnerabilities (CVE-2024-47177, CVE-2024-47176, CVE-2024-47076, CVE-2024-47175). Watch for abnormal child process creation, unexpected file writes, or modifications by the cupsd process. Block external access to UDP port 631 and review system and application logs for signs of exploitation, such as unauthorized configuration changes or execution of unknown binaries by the CUPS service.
